title: Ingress, Gateway API and the load balancer GKE creates for you

videos.script: One line in a Kubernetes manifest, and Google builds a load balancer in your project. This lesson is about which one, and what it costs you to get the choice wrong. {{service}} A Service of type LoadBalancer gets a layer four load balancer. It sees connections, not requests. Each Service gets its own address. {{ingress}} An Ingress gets an Application Load Balancer. One global address, many paths, and a certificate Google renews. You reserve the address first, so it never moves. {{neg}} Then the hop nobody sees. The old way sent every request through a node. The new way sends it straight to the pod. {{gateway}} Last, the Gateway API. It splits the load balancer from the routes, so each team owns its own. And it can send one request in ten to a new version.
